text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has suspended 87 senior civil servants on charges of corruption and indiscipline, the government said on Thursday.
The officials, who now face more inquiries and possible dismissals, include seven top bureaucrats, heads of state-run banks and a former intelligence chief, government sources said.
"These officers are being suspended on charges of corruption, reputation of being corrupt or on reports of having acted in wilful disregard of service discipline," the statement said.

Government sources said among the suspended officials were former Commerce Ministry secretary Salman Faruqui, who was known to be close to former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari, and his brother Usman Faruqui, ex-chairman of the state-run Pakistan Steel Mills under Bhutto's government.

They said also suspended was former Intelligence Bureau chief Masood Sharif and former Federal Investigation Agency police chief Ghulam Asghar, both of whom had been accused in the past of harassing Bhutto's political opponents.

Among other suspended men are former Petroleum Ministry secretary Captain Naseer, ex-chairman of state-run Oil and Gas Development Corp Riffat Askari, two former chiefs of state-run National Bank of Pakistan, Abu Saeed Islahi and M.B. Abbassi, and former president of Habib Bank Ltd Younas Dalia.
The government statement said the action had been taken in line with Sharif's commitment to root out corruption from government departments.

"The suspended officers would have a right to defend themselves against the corruption charges," it said. "The government is committed to the process of accountability but would ensure that no injustice is done to anyone."
